reading.title: The Hidden Toll of Traffic Noise
reading.intro_zh: 这篇拓展阅读不复述机场原文，而是转向一个真实的公共卫生话题：交通噪音对身体健康的隐性影响，内容改编自权威期刊《Environmental Health Perspectives》。

source.title: Environmental Noise Pollution in the United States: Developing an Effective Public Health Response

passage: When a new motorway opens or an airport finally comes into use, the surrounding neighbourhoods rarely fall silent again. The roar of engines and the hum of tyres settle over nearby homes night and day, and researchers now treat this constant background sound as far more than a nuisance. Public-health scientists describe transportation noise as an environmental stressor, meaning a force that the body registers and reacts to even when a person is asleep or no longer consciously listening. The main sources are familiar ones: road and rail traffic, air transport, and the machinery of industry.

The consequences are surprisingly physical. According to one review in Environmental Health Perspectives, an estimated 104 million Americans were exposed to yearly noise levels above 70 decibels in 2013, while roughly 145 million faced a possible raised risk of hypertension. The mechanism is gradual rather than dramatic. Repeated noise fragments sleep, elevates stress hormones, and over time can damage blood vessels and raise blood pressure, which is why chronic exposure has been linked to heart disease. Children are affected too, with studies reporting weaker reading comprehension and shorter concentration where noise is severe.

Regulation, however, has lagged behind the evidence. The United States once ran a dedicated Office of Noise Abatement and Control, but it was effectively driven away by budget cuts after only a decade, and federal guidance has remained largely frozen since. Experts therefore argue that the 55-decibel residential threshold, set to protect against adverse effects, deserves renewed attention. For the families who stay put rather than accept relocation, the lesson is sobering: the quietest hours of the day may be doing the loudest damage.

questions.question: What is the main point of the passage?
options: Airports are noisier than motorways and should be closed.
Noise is only a problem for people who choose not to move away.
Transportation noise is a genuine public-health threat, not merely an annoyance.
Children sleep better near busy roads than adults do.
questions.explanation_zh: 全文反复强调交通噪音被科学家视为一种 environmental stressor，会真正影响身体健康，而不仅仅是“吵”。这是文章的核心论点。

questions.question: According to the review cited, what was true of noise exposure in the United States in 2013?
options: About 104 million Americans were exposed to yearly noise levels above 70 decibels.
Only people living next to airports were affected by harmful noise.
Noise levels had fallen below the 55-decibel residential threshold.
Fewer than ten million Americans faced any risk of hypertension.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段明确指出 an estimated 104 million Americans were exposed to yearly noise levels above 70 decibels in 2013。

questions.question: How does chronic noise lead to cardiovascular harm, according to the passage?
options: It directly damages the heart muscle on the first night of exposure.
It makes people exercise less because they stay indoors.
It forces families to move, raising their stress about money.
It fragments sleep and raises stress hormones, which over time can damage blood vessels and raise blood pressure.
questions.explanation_zh: 第二段描述了渐进的机制：噪音 fragments sleep, elevates stress hormones, and over time can damage blood vessels and raise blood pressure，从而与心脏病相关。

questions.question: What can be inferred about U.S. noise regulation from the final paragraph?
options: It has kept pace with the latest scientific findings.
It has fallen behind the evidence and remained largely unchanged for years.
It was strengthened after the Office of Noise Abatement and Control closed.
It now bans all residential noise above 55 decibels nationwide.
questions.explanation_zh: 末段说监管 has lagged behind the evidence，相关办公室被预算削减取消，联邦指导 remained largely frozen，可推断监管落后且多年未更新。

questions.question: In the passage, the word "sobering" most nearly means:
options: amusing and lighthearted
confusing and unclear
making one think seriously about something worrying
completely false or exaggerated
questions.explanation_zh: sobering 在文中形容这个结论让人警醒、严肃思考一个令人担忧的事实（最安静的时段反而伤害最大），因此意为“发人深省的、令人警醒的”。

writing.intro_zh: 今天把 Lesson 21 的五个核心句式提升到 B2+ 难度：用被动写无法逃避的声音，用 for some reason 说明原因不明，用 came into use 写设施投入运营，用 have been offered 写收到的正式提议，用 determined to 写压力下的坚定抉择。每句都要更抽象、更复杂，但仍要保留被动语态等语法重点。

patterns.title: can be heard night and day
patterns.source: Passing planes can be heard night and day.
patterns.focus_zh: 用被动语态写一种无法躲开的声音：重点不是谁在听，而是这种声音一直存在。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：用被动语态描写一种无法躲开、令人疲惫的声音（施工、交通或机器声）日夜不断地侵入人们的生活。
patterns.sample: The relentless drone of the new ring road can be heard night and day, seeping into every bedroom along the street.
patterns.tip_zh: can be heard 后面直接接声音出现的时间或地点；night and day 比 all day 更有压迫感。

patterns.title: for some reason
patterns.source: For some reason, it could not be used then.
patterns.focus_zh: for some reason 用来说明“由于某种原因”，原因不清楚或不想展开。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：某项工程、设备或制度由于某种说不清的原因迟迟无法正常运作或被使用。
patterns.sample: For some reason that the authorities never bothered to explain, the newly completed bridge could not be opened to the public.
patterns.tip_zh: for some reason 可以放在句首，也可以放在句中；后面要把结果说清楚。

patterns.title: came into use
patterns.source: Last year, however, it came into use.
patterns.focus_zh: came into use 表示一个地方、系统或设备开始被使用、开始运营。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：一项历经波折、耗资巨大的基础设施或系统在长期等待后终于投入使用。
patterns.sample: After years of costly delays and political wrangling, the high-speed rail line finally came into use last autumn.
patterns.tip_zh: 主语通常是 facility 或 system，例如 road, bridge, station, app；不要写成 people came into use。

patterns.title: have been offered
patterns.source: I have been offered a large sum of money to go away.
patterns.focus_zh: have been offered 用被动语态写“已经收到某个提议”，重点在收到提议的人。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：某些人已经被提供一笔可观的补偿或一个重要选择，但他们的态度复杂、并不轻易接受。
patterns.sample: Several long-term residents have been offered substantial compensation to relocate, yet many remain deeply reluctant to leave.
patterns.tip_zh: 这个结构不等于已经接受；只是说明 offer 已经被提出。

patterns.title: determined to ...
patterns.source: I am determined to stay here.
patterns.focus_zh: determined to 表示在压力下仍然下定决心做某事。
patterns.task_zh: 仿写一句：在巨大的外部压力或他人反对下，某人仍然坚定地决心去守护、完成或坚持某件重要的事。
patterns.sample: Despite the mounting noise and pressure from her neighbours, she remains stubbornly determined to defend the home she grew up in.
patterns.tip_zh: determined to 后面接动词原形；句子最好带出一点压力，选择才有重量。
